newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sonatrach details $19.3 bln Algeria oil and gas plan.
newsitem.headline: Sonatrach details $19.3 bln Algeria oil and gas plan.

text.p: Algerian state energy firm Sonatrach and its foreign partners are planning to invest $19.3 billion in the north African's oil and gas sectors up to the year 2001 in a move which will boost Algeria's petroleum exports, a senior Sonatrach official said on Wednesday.

Mourad Preure, adviser to Sonatrach's director general, told an energy conference in Dubai that some $12 billion would be spent on oil and gas field development and $3.3 billion on pipeline transportation over the next four years.
This investment was expected to increase Algerian crude production to 1.3 million barrels per day (bpd) from 800,000 bpd and condensate output to 460,000 bpd from 400,000 bpd.
OPEC-member Algeria has a current supply quota of 750,000 bpd though independent assessments estimate that it is producing around 850,000 bpd.

Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) exports would rise to to eight million tonnes a year from 3.9 million tonnes and a doubling of natural gas exports, Preure said in a paper delivered to the Middle East Pipeline Congress.
Algeria exported 41 billion cubic metres of gas in 1996, 51 percent in the form of natural gas and 49 percent as liquefied natural gas (LNG), Preure's conference paper showed.

Algeria's total hydrocarbon reserves base stood at 36 billion barrels of oil equivalent, mostly of natural gas (57 percent), crude oil (27 percent), condensate (nine percent) and liquefied petroleum gas (seven percent).

Sixty percent of the $19.3 billion planned investment or some $11.6 billion would be in foreign currency with Sonatrach contributing $6.02 billion in hard currency amd the remainder by foreign partners.
